Canadian dude here. As you may remember there was a time when we Canadians loved referendums.

Referendums are generally useless, I hate to say. As democratic as they may seem at face value, ultimately, unless they are backed up by some kind of legislation they are ineffective.

Also, the population at large are generally uninformed by the totality of what they are voting for and will generally vote emotionally. This will pretty much always lead to a referendum ending up at a near 50/50 split between yea or nay. Because you'll have 50% of happy people and 50% of scared people with a small percentage swinging one way or the other.

Also, what constitutes a "win" for one side or the other? Is it 50% + 1? Is it 51%? It's ridiculous to think that the politicos would ignore the wishes of 49.9% of the population especially if the referendum is based around something that will cause a BIG departure from the staus-quo. Therefore, you'll find that even if the "leave" side wins, the arguments will arise that it wasn't by a significant majority. They'll argue vote-count error possibilities, they'll argue that it's not a significant majority vote --- so unless you get 65% or more voting in one way, I'd suspect the politicos would just toss the referendum results out as a tie. And 65%+ would be near impossible to get, because of people voting with emotions.

This is why it needs to have clear legislation behind it which clearly defines what a "win" is and also clearly defines what the standing government must do within a defined period of time if the referendum comes back.

All recent referendums which come to my mind inevitably have landed at near 50/50 ties, i.e., useless wastes of time and efforts.
